text:
Visitors to Korea’s capital now have more time to take in its glittering winter skyline, as city extends evening hours at Seoul City Hall Sky Observatory downtown and opens the panoramic viewing deck on Sundays for the first time this season.
The expanded schedule will run from Dec. 11, 2026, through Feb. 9, 2027, coinciding with the Seoul Winter Festa and the operation of the Seoul Plaza ice rink, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said.
The observatory, located on the eighth and ninth floors of Seoul City Hall’s main building, will remain open until 9 p.m. Monday through Thursday and Sunday, and until 10 p.m. Friday and Saturday.
Special hours will allow visitors to stay until midnight on Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve, while the observatory will close at 10 p.m. on Christmas Day.
The observatory will operate from 7:30 a.m. to 9 p.m. Monday through Thursday, from 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. Friday and Saturday, and from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. Sunday.
The extended schedule is intended to give residents and tourists more opportunities to enjoy views of central Seoul during the busy winter festival period, the city said.
The observatory offers free admission and requires no reservations, with views of landmarks including Deoksu Palace and Seoul Anglican Cathedral.
Visitors can reach the eighth and ninth floors through a dedicated elevator next to the robot cafe on the first floor of Seoul City Hall’s main building.
The expanded hours follow strong public interest since the observatory opened July 7, with 196,494 visitors recorded through Wednesday, according to the city.
That amounts to an average of 1,913 visitors per operating day, while the busiest day drew 3,836 people on Oct. 10.
Evening visits averaged 2,480 people per day, compared with 1,631 during weekday daytime hours, underscoring the appeal of the nighttime views.
The city also plans to hold a visitor contest in December, inviting submissions of photographs, paintings, poems and videos inspired by the observatory and its surrounding views, with awards scheduled for February.
Kwak Jong-bin, head of the Seoul Metropolitan Government’s Administrative Bureau, said the observatory had quickly become a popular new viewing destination.
“The Sky Observatory has earned the affection of many citizens and tourists in a short period and is establishing itself as a new scenic attraction in Seoul,” Kwak said.
“We will extend its opening hours this winter so more citizens and tourists can enjoy the beautiful nighttime views of the city center, and continue developing it into a space that showcases new attractions of Seoul,” he said.
This article was published with the assistance of generative AI and edited by The Korea Times.
